text:
ashley: seeing a spike of outbound failures from bastions and some GPU nodes in us-east-1 since ~02:10 UTC. 500s for package pulls and intermittent agent webhooks. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/egress-ports :eyes:
ben: same. noticed a sharp rise in NAT ActiveConnections and a matching surge in TIME_WAIT on the hosts.
carmen: any recent deploys that would open a ton of outbound connections?
ashley: we rolled a bulk model-puller change yesterday that spreads downloads across nodes (intended). probably increased concurrent TCP churn.
devops-bot: CloudWatch alert: NATGateway-ue1-a ActiveSockets=62000 (threshold 60000) at 02:14 UTC. NATGateway-ue1-b at 58500.
raj: that's basically 64k ephemeral ports per NAT. once you hit that, new SNATs fail. symptoms: outbound hangs, connection resets, higher client 502s.
tim: can we confirm per-node conntrack counts? quick check: `sudo ss -s` and `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`
ben: ran quick on one gpu-node-3: `ss -s` shows ~32k established/closing, `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` => `32768 60999`
carmen: that range is okay but with many short-lived connections you still hit port scarcity. Also TIME_WAIT pile-up because apps aren't reusing keep-alives.
ashley: past postmortems suggested two options: (1) add more NATs (per-AZ) or (2) introduce an egress-proxy that does connection pooling. both have tradeoffs.
raj: adding NATs quick fix: create additional NAT gateways in the other subnet and update route tables per private subnet. costy but immediate.
tim: egress-proxy helps long term. run squid/nginx as HTTP CONNECT proxy in each AZ, have nodes route 80/443 via it or use iptables redirect for http(s) from app tier. proxies reuse connections to external hosts.
ben: short checklist I ran:
```
# count TIME_WAIT
sudo ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l
# conntrack (if available)
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count || echo no-conntrack
```
ashley: observed `TIME_WAIT` ~28k on the node, conntrack not present (we're on managed AMI).
carmen: we also saw a bunch of ephemeral port reuse warnings in the edge proxy logs: `snat_port_exhaustion: allocate() failed`.
devops-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-183900 (egress port saturation, us-east-1).
raj: mitigation plan: 1) create two extra NAT gateways in us-east-1 (az-a, az-c) and update route tables (owner: ben) 2) force model-puller backoff to 10s jittered (owner: ashley) 3) roll egress-proxy canary to one GPU node pool with connection pooling (owner: tim) 4) add alert for NAT ActiveConnections > 55k (owner: carmen)
tim: adding proxy is non-trivial for TLS. either do transparent TLS termination (not acceptable) or HTTP CONNECT/CONNECT keepalive so TLS stays end-to-end. we'll prefer CONNECT.
ben: I'm provisioning NATs now. ETA ~15m for route table changes. I'll also enable cross-zone outbound balancing.
ashley: rolling model-puller throttle now. starting canary at 02:36 UTC.
carmen: action: add a quick Grafana panel showing ephemeral port usage (TIME_WAIT + Active connections) and tag services with egress profiles so we can prioritize critical traffic over model pulls.
ben: deployed new NATs. ActiveConnections dropped to ~42k after route changes and pulling throttled. 502s dropped. :thumbsup:
raj: follow-ups: - make egress-proxy run as sidecar for heavy-download workflows - add per-service egress quotas - consider using S3 multipart for model artifacts to reduce new TCP handshakes - evaluate AWS PrivateLink for model registry to avoid NAT entirely.
ashley: thanks team. I'll open a retrospective doc and schedule a small RFC for egress-proxy design next week. cc @tim @ben for implementation notes.
tim: will draft config for CONNECT pooling and share. expect some app tweaks for long-lived client reuse.
devops-bot: Incident INC-2026-183900 resolved at 02:44 UTC.
ashley: closing thread, will follow up in RFC. :white_check_mark:
